requirements.quote:
A security-aware resolver can use an RRSIG RR to authenticate an
   RRset if all of the following conditions hold:

   o  The RRSIG RR and the RRset MUST have the same owner name and the
      same class.
requirements.condition: A security-aware resolver uses an RRSIG RR to authenticate an RRset; this check applies together with all of the listed RRSIG validity conditions.
requirements.required_behavior: The RRSIG RR and the RRset MUST have the same owner name.
requirements.why_checkable: The RRSIG owner name can be compared with the owner name of the RRset being authenticated.

A security-aware resolver can use an RRSIG RR to authenticate an
   RRset if all of the following conditions hold:

   o  The RRSIG RR and the RRset MUST have the same owner name and the
      same class.

   o  The RRSIG RR's Signer's Name field MUST be the name of the zone
      that contains the RRset.

   o  The RRSIG RR's Type Covered field MUST equal the RRset's type.

   o  The number of labels in the RRset owner name MUST be greater than
      or equal to the value in the RRSIG RR's Labels field.

   o  The validator's notion of the current time MUST be less than or
      equal to the time listed in the RRSIG RR's Expiration field.

   o  The validator's notion of the current time MUST be greater than or
      equal to the time listed in the RRSIG RR's Inception field.

   o  The RRSIG RR's Signer's Name, Algorithm, and Key Tag fields MUST
      match the owner name, algorithm, and key tag for some DNSKEY RR in
      the zone's apex DNSKEY RRset.
requirements.condition: A security-aware resolver uses an RRSIG RR to authenticate an RRset; this check applies together with all of the listed RRSIG validity conditions. All Signer's Name, Algorithm, and Key Tag comparisons must be satisfied together by one and the same candidate DNSKEY RR in the zone's apex DNSKEY RRset.
requirements.required_behavior: The RRSIG RR's Signer's Name field MUST match the owner name of that same candidate DNSKEY RR.
requirements.why_checkable: A candidate-key lookup can be checked for owner-name equality and for retaining the same candidate across the algorithm and key-tag checks.

requirements.quote:
A security-aware resolver can use an RRSIG RR to authenticate an
   RRset if all of the following conditions hold:

   o  The RRSIG RR and the RRset MUST have the same owner name and the
      same class.

   o  The RRSIG RR's Signer's Name field MUST be the name of the zone
      that contains the RRset.

   o  The RRSIG RR's Type Covered field MUST equal the RRset's type.

   o  The number of labels in the RRset owner name MUST be greater than
      or equal to the value in the RRSIG RR's Labels field.

   o  The validator's notion of the current time MUST be less than or
      equal to the time listed in the RRSIG RR's Expiration field.

   o  The validator's notion of the current time MUST be greater than or
      equal to the time listed in the RRSIG RR's Inception field.

   o  The RRSIG RR's Signer's Name, Algorithm, and Key Tag fields MUST
      match the owner name, algorithm, and key tag for some DNSKEY RR in
      the zone's apex DNSKEY RRset.

   o  The matching DNSKEY RR MUST be present in the zone's apex DNSKEY
      RRset, and MUST have the Zone Flag bit (DNSKEY RDATA Flag bit 7)
      set.
requirements.condition: A security-aware resolver uses an RRSIG RR to authenticate an RRset; this check applies together with all of the listed RRSIG validity conditions. All Signer's Name, Algorithm, and Key Tag comparisons must be satisfied together by one and the same candidate DNSKEY RR in the zone's apex DNSKEY RRset.
requirements.required_behavior: The same matching DNSKEY RR MUST be present in the zone's apex DNSKEY RRset.
requirements.why_checkable: The source RRset of each matching candidate key can be checked for membership in the zone apex DNSKEY RRset.

All Signer's Name, Algorithm, and Key Tag comparisons must be satisfied together by one and the same candidate DNSKEY RR in the zone's apex DNSKEY RRset.
requirements.required_behavior: The same matching DNSKEY RR MUST have its Zone Flag bit, DNSKEY RDATA Flag bit 7, set.
requirements.why_checkable: The Zone Flag bit can be inspected on the same DNSKEY record that satisfies the signature-field matching conditions.

requirements.quote:
o  The RRSIG RR's Signer's Name, Algorithm, and Key Tag fields MUST
      match the owner name, algorithm, and key tag for some DNSKEY RR in
      the zone's apex DNSKEY RRset.

   o  The matching DNSKEY RR MUST be present in the zone's apex DNSKEY
      RRset, and MUST have the Zone Flag bit (DNSKEY RDATA Flag bit 7)
      set.





Arends, et al.              Standards Track                    [Page 28]


RFC 4035             DNSSEC Protocol Modifications            March 2005


   It is possible for more than one DNSKEY RR to match the conditions
   above.  In this case, the validator cannot predetermine which DNSKEY
   RR to use to authenticate the signature, and it MUST try each
   matching DNSKEY RR until either the signature is validated or the
   validator has run out of matching public keys to try.
requirements.condition: More than one DNSKEY RR matches the listed conditions: the RRSIG Signer's Name, Algorithm, and Key Tag match the owner name, algorithm, and key tag of the same DNSKEY RR, which is in the zone's apex DNSKEY RRset and has the Zone Flag bit set.
requirements.required_behavior: The validator MUST try each matching DNSKEY RR until the signature is validated or no matching public keys remain to try.
requirements.why_checkable: A signature with several matching key candidates can establish whether validation continues after an unsuccessful candidate and terminates on success or candidate exhaustion.

requirements.condition: A validator uses a DNSKEY RR to validate signatures as part of this authentication process.
requirements.required_behavior: Authenticate the DNSKEY RR before using it to validate signatures, as the stated prerequisite for meaningful authentication.
requirements.why_checkable: The authentication state of the selected DNSKEY and its ordering relative to signature validation can be inspected.

   o  the apex DNSKEY RRset containing the DNSKEY RR is considered

requirements.condition: The apex DNSKEY RRset containing the matching DNSKEY RR is considered authentic.
requirements.required_behavior: Consider the matching DNSKEY RR authentic under this sufficient alternative.
requirements.why_checkable: A matching key in an authenticated apex DNSKEY RRset has a directly checkable resulting authentication status.

requirements.quote:
Note that this authentication process is only meaningful if the
   validator authenticates the DNSKEY RR before using it to validate
   signatures.  The matching DNSKEY RR is considered to be authentic if:

   o  the apex DNSKEY RRset containing the DNSKEY RR is considered
      authentic; or

   o  the RRset covered by the RRSIG RR is the apex DNSKEY RRset itself,
      and the DNSKEY RR either matches an authenticated DS RR from the
      parent zone or matches a trust anchor.
requirements.condition: The RRset covered by the RRSIG RR is the apex DNSKEY RRset itself, and the same matching DNSKEY RR matches an authenticated DS RR from the parent zone.
requirements.required_behavior: Consider the matching DNSKEY RR authentic under this sufficient alternative.
requirements.why_checkable: The covered RRset identity, the parent DS authentication state, the match of that DS to the same DNSKEY, and the resulting DNSKEY authentication status can be inspected together.
